Observed at +0.17604613304138184s — page 1
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:13:`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers
, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the ru
n with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it
uses your existing CLI login and billing.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:23:With results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in th
e authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new
run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client pro
file is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no pr
ompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Re
tries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, o
r balance refusal.

/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:136:There is no fallback: a key the provider rejects is a credential failure (exit `3`)
, never a reason to spend platform credits instead.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:140:MCPJam-hosted inference uses the Cloud credential precedence (`--api-key` > `MCPJAM
_API_KEY` > `mcpjam cloud login`) and project precedence (`--project` > `MCPJAM_PROJECT` > `mcpjam cloud link` > most recently upd
ated), plus `--api-url` / `--api-header`. The platform is contacted only when a selected case needs it. Hosted inference still mak
es inference and billing requests; "no upload" means no eval results or artifacts are ever sent.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:144:`--host <template>` emulates one existing host template — its `initialize` identity
, advertised capabilities, protocol versions and tool visibility, plus its model settings where the suite does not set them. It ne
ver launches the real client, and reports say "emulated". The suite's model, and any authored `systemPrompt` / `temperature`, win
over the template's. `target.hosts` in the file is recorded as declared but not executed, and `target.environment` as declared but
not resolved.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:185:| Prompt steps (including several per case) | Run as one conversation per iteration
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:187:| Direct `toolCall` steps | Refused before anything runs — use a prompt, or run hos
ted |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:194:Every selected case is checked before any model or tool call, so an unsupported lat
er case costs nothing. Hosted-only capabilities run with `mcpjam cloud eval run --file <file>`.

or a report that could not be written |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/local-evals.md:225:This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a devel
oper documentation platform.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:27:One scenario you want to verify — a prompt (or a sequence of prompts), the tools you expec
t to fire, an optional expected output, and the assertions that decide pass/fail.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:45:* **Prompt** — a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **A
dd assertion or action** to add a second prompt for multi-turn cases.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:53:Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertion, a second prompt, or an interact step.
Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:110:6. **Empty** — no trial yet; start typing a prompt.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:114:> A **negative case** is one you marked **No tool should be called**. Meta questions ("wh
at params does `search` take?"), conversational drift, and ambiguous prompts are the usual shape. A case that simply names no tool
is *not* negative — it is graded by its assertions.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:143:When attachments are present, a note is automatically prepended to the case's first user
turn listing each file's path, so the model knows where to find them without you having to mention it in the prompt.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:155:Click **Start recording** in the case spine. The button is disabled until the prompt is n
on-empty — type a prompt first, then start recording. Once active, a recorder shim is injected into the widget sandbox. Every clic
k and text input you make in the widget is captured as a locator-stable `interact` step and appended to the case. The locator is b
uilt from stable identifiers in priority order: `data-testid` → ARIA role + accessible name → visible text → CSS path. This means
the recorded step resolves to the same element when the case runs headlessly.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:163:This means an eval case can faithfully verify a full widget interaction sequence: prompt
→ widget renders → user clicks → model reacts → tool fires → assertion passes.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:189:A run that never uses a browser tool records nothing, and costs nothing.
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:208:| **Token budget under N** | Total token usage stayed below the cap. | Case only |
/workspace/mcpjam-eval/docs/evals.md:210:When an assertion is authored on an individual prompt turn it is evaluated against **that
turn's slice** of the transcript — tool calls, assistant message, tool errors, and widget observations for that turn only. `Token
budget under N` is case-only because per-turn token usage is not reliably captured; all other assertions are turn-scopable.
